pages.text: Omar has a red magnet. It can pull things!
It picks up a spoon. It can't pick up a ball!
Grandpa is sad. "My key is in the grass. Where is it?"
"I can help, Grandpa!" Omar puts the magnet on a long stick.
Click! The key jumps to the magnet.
Grandpa smiles. "Thank you, Omar. You are a scientist!"

questions.q: What can the magnet pick up?
Why does Omar put the magnet on a long stick?
options: To find the key in the grass

pages.text: Noura and Grandpa are in the desert. The sand is hot and yellow.
"Grandpa, where is the baby camel?" "Oh no! I don't know!"
"Look, Grandpa! Little camel feet in the sand! Let's go!"
They walk to a big rock. "Listen! What's that?"
The baby camel is behind the rock! Noura gives it water.
They walk home together. Mama Camel is very happy!

questions.q: Why is Mama Camel very happy?

pages.text: Grandpa has got a big hat. The hat is on the table.
"Look! The hat is moving!" says Omar.
"Is it a monster?" asks Mona. "I don't know!" says Grandpa.
The hat jumps! Now it is on the floor.
Grandpa looks under the hat. A little kitten says, "Meow!"
Grandpa laughs. "Nice hat, kitten! It is your hat now!"

questions.q: Where is the hat at the start?
Who says the hat is moving?

pages.text: Omar and Grandpa are on a boat. The sea is big and blue.
"Look, Grandpa! A turtle!" "Oh no, Omar. It can't swim."
There is a bag on the turtle. Omar takes the bag.
The turtle swims away. "Bye, turtle!"
Then the turtle comes back. A baby turtle comes, too!
Omar puts the bag in the bin. "No bags in the sea!"

questions.q: Who comes back with the turtle?

pages.text: Oh no! Omar's red ball is in the tall tree.
Omar is small. The tree is very tall.
Omar has a long stick, a cup and some tape.
"Look, Mona! I can make a ball catcher!"
Up, up, up! Yes! The ball is in the cup!
Mona smiles. "Omar, you are an inventor!"

questions.q: Where is the ball at the start?
What does Omar use to make the ball catcher?
options: a stick, a cup and some tape

questions.q: Why can't Omar get the ball with his hands?
options: He is small and the tree is tall.

pages.text: We are at the airport. Look at the big plane!
I sit by the window. The clouds are white and soft.
Now we are in a new city. Where is my blue bag?
Oh no! There are ten blue bags!
Dad smiles. "Your bag has a yellow star, Omar."
I see it! This is my bag. Now let's go to Grandma's house!

questions.q: Where are Omar and Dad at the start?
How many blue bags are there?
How does Omar find his bag?

pages.text: This is Yusuf. He is small, but he can run fast.
The big boys play football in the park. "Can I play?" Yusuf asks.
"No, you are too small!" says Khalid. Yusuf is sad.
Oh no! The ball goes far, far away. The big boys are slow.
Yusuf runs fast. He kicks the ball. Goal!
"Wow! Please play with us, Yusuf!" says Khalid. Yusuf smiles.

questions.q: Where do the big boys play football?

options: The boys say he is too small.

questions.q: How does Khalid feel about Yusuf at the end?
options: He thinks Yusuf is a good player.
He wants Yusuf to go home.

stories.title: Big Bip and the Small Cat

pages.text: This is Bip. Bip is a big, blue robot.
Bip can carry a car! Bip is very strong.
Look! A small, white cat. Bip is scared!
Sara laughs. "Bip, it is only a cat!"
The cat jumps on Bip. "Meow!" says the cat.
Now the cat sleeps on Bip's head. Bip is happy!

questions.q: At the end, is the cat Bip's friend?
options: Yes, it sleeps on Bip's head.

pages.text: Sara and Grandpa walk in the desert. The sand is hot and yellow.
Sara sees something small. "Grandpa, look! What's this?"
"It's a coin," says Grandpa. "It's very, very old!"
They take the coin to the museum. A kind woman looks at it.
"Wow! This coin is from an old market," she says. "Thank you, Sara!"
Now the coin is in a glass box. A card says: "From Sara."

questions.q: Where do Sara and Grandpa walk?
What does "old" mean in the story?
Where is the coin at the end?
Why does the woman say "Thank you, Sara"?
options: Sara gives the coin to the museum

pages.text: "Look, Dad! A baby turtle on the beach!" says Sara.
The turtle is very small. It walks to the car lights, not to the sea.
"Oh no! The sea is here, little turtle!" says Omar.
Dad turns off the car lights. Now the turtle can see the moon on the sea.
The turtle walks and walks. Sara and Omar walk with it.
Splash! The turtle swims in the sea. "Goodbye, little friend!"

questions.q: Where does the turtle walk first?

options: He turns off the car lights

questions.q: Why does Dad turn off the lights?
options: So the turtle can find the sea

pages.text: It is Friday morning. Dad is sleeping.
Sara and Ali are in the kitchen. "Let's cook breakfast for Dad!"
Ali has three eggs. Oops! The eggs fall on the floor!
"Oh no! No eggs!" says Ali. "I know! Fruit salad!" says Sara.
Mum helps. They cut bananas, apples and oranges, and they put dates on top.
Dad comes to the kitchen. "Wow! It's yummy! Thank you!"

questions.q: Why do Sara and Ali make fruit salad?
How does Dad feel at the end?

0-2.q: This is my friend. ___ name is Tom.
I am eight. Ben is eight. He is eight ___.

0-4.q: Have you got a sister? No, I ___.

1-1.q: Is this your bag? Yes, it ___.

options: No, it isn't. It's his ruler.

1-2.answer: My pen is red and blue.

1-2.q: What colour is your ruler? It's ___.

options: My bag is blue and green.
My is bag blue and green.

1-4.answer: Can I have a rubber, please?

1-4.q: Can I have a pencil, please?

options: Can I have a crayon, please?
Can I a crayon have, please?
I can have a crayon, please?

2-1.answer: For breakfast I have eggs and bread.

2-2.answer: Can I have some juice, please?

2-2.q: Can I have some water, please? ___

options: Can I has some milk, please?
Can I have some milk, please?
Can me have some milk, please?

2-4.answer: I'd like a mango juice, please.

options: I'd like a banana juice, please.

3-1.q: What colour is the camel? — It's ___.

3-3.answer: Has it got a long tail?

options: Has it got a long neck?
Is it got a long neck?
Has it a got long neck?

3-4.answer: My pet is small and white.

3-4.q: I've got a dog. ___ name is Max.
I haven't got a pet. I ___ a rabbit.

3-5.answer: My favourite animal is the tiger.

options: My favourite animal is the giraffe.

dialogue.t: This is my brother. His name is Sami.

grammar.title: This is my... / He is / She is
grammar.ar: نستخدم "This is my..." لنُعرّف شخصًا ونشير إليه، ومعناها "هذا/هذه ...ـي". نستخدم "He" للمذكر بمعنى "هو"، و"She" للمؤنث بمعنى "هي". بعد he وshe نضع دائمًا "is".

dialogue.t: And how old is your sister?
I'm eight. How old are you?

grammar.title: Asking about age: How old...?
grammar.ar: نسأل عن العمر بـ "How old is your...?" ومعناها "كم عمر ...؟". نجيب بـ "He is" أو "She is" ثم الرقم، ويمكن أن نضيف "years old" في النهاية. انتبه: نستخدم "is" مع العمر، ولا نقول "He has ten years".

words.ex: I'm eight. He is eight too.

dialogue.t: My best friend is a boy. His name is Omar.
He is eight. I'm eight too.
My best friend is a girl. Her name is Lina.

grammar.title: His / Her and too
grammar.ar: نستخدم "His" للمذكر بمعنى "ـهُ" مثل "اسمُه"، ونستخدم "Her" للمؤنث بمعنى "ـها" مثل "اسمُها". كلمة "too" تعني "أيضًا" وتأتي في آخر الجملة.

dialogue.t: No, he isn't. He is my uncle.
No, she isn't. My aunt is short.

grammar.title: Is he tall? Yes, he is. / No, he isn't.
grammar.ar: لنسأل سؤالًا جوابه نعم أو لا، نضع "Is" في بداية الجملة قبل he أو she. نجيب إجابة قصيرة: "Yes, he is" أو "No, he isn't". كلمة "isn't" اختصار لـ "is not" وتعني "ليس".
examples: Is she short? Yes, she is.
Is he tall? No, he isn't.

dialogue.t: Yes, I have. I've got two sisters.
No, I haven't. Have you got a brother?
Yes, I have. I've got one brother.

grammar.title: Have you got...? / I've got...
grammar.ar: نستخدم "have got" بمعنى "عندي" أو "لديّ". للسؤال نقول "Have you got a...?" ونجيب "Yes, I have" أو "No, I haven't". "I've" اختصار لـ "I have". عندما يكون العدد أكثر من واحد نضيف s للكلمة مثل two brothers.

words.ex: Hello, Uncle Sami! How are you?

dialogue.t: I'm fine, thank you. How are you?
Aunt Huda, this is my friend Ali.
Nice to meet you, Ali. Welcome!
And this is my cousin Sara.
Hello, Sara! Nice to meet you.

grammar.title: Polite greetings and introductions
grammar.ar: نبدأ بـ "Hello" ثم اسم الشخص. لنُعرّف شخصًا نقول "This is my...". عندما نقابل شخصًا لأول مرة نقول "Nice to meet you". وإذا سألنا أحد "How are you?" نجيب بأدب "I'm fine, thank you".

words.ex: My pencil case is in my bag.

dialogue.t: Let's look! I've got a book.
It's my pencil case. I've got two pencils.
I've got a rubber and two pens.
Wow! I've got a pen too.

grammar.title: I've got a ... / I've got two ...
grammar.ar: نستخدم "I've got" لنقول ماذا نملك، ومعناها "عندي". مع الشيء الواحد نضع "a" قبل الاسم مثل: a pen. ومع أكثر من شيء نضع العدد ونضيف حرف "s" في آخر الاسم مثل: two pens.
examples: What's in your bag? I've got three pencils.

words.ex: Is this your pen? Yes, it is.
Is this your rubber? No, it isn't.

dialogue.t: Look! A pencil. Is this your pencil?
No, it isn't. It's his pencil.
Oh, OK. Is this your ruler?
And this bag? Is this your bag?
No, it isn't. It's her bag.

grammar.title: Is this your ...? / his / her
grammar.ar: نسأل "Is this your ...?" لنعرف هل الشيء ملك الشخص الذي نكلمه. الجواب القصير يكون "Yes, it is." أو "No, it isn't.". نستخدم "his" للولد و"her" للبنت لنقول لمن هذا الشيء.
examples: Is this your book? Yes, it is.
Is this your pen? No, it isn't.
It's his ruler. It's her rubber.

words.ex: My bag is black and red.

dialogue.t: What colour is your pencil case?
It's blue. What colour is your bag?
My bag is green and yellow.
I like it! What colour is your ruler?

grammar.title: What colour is ...? / It's ...
grammar.ar: نسأل عن لون الشيء بقولنا "What colour is your ...?". نجيب بقولنا "It's" ثم اسم اللون مثل: It's red. وإذا كان للشيء لونان نستخدم "and" بينهما مثل: My bag is blue and black.
examples: What colour is your pen? It's black.
My pencil is red and yellow.

words.ex: The book is on the desk.
The ruler is under the chair.
My pen is on the desk.
The bag is under the chair.
The crayons are in the box.

dialogue.t: Oh no! Where is my ruler?
Thank you! Where is the book?

grammar.title: Where is the ...? / in, on, under
grammar.ar: نسأل عن مكان الشيء بقولنا "Where is the ...?". نجيب بـ "It's" ثم كلمة المكان: "in" تعني داخل، و"on" تعني على، و"under" تعني تحت. لا ننسى كلمة "the" قبل اسم المكان مثل: in the bag.
examples: Where is the pen? It's in the bag.
The book is on the desk.
The rubber is under the chair.

words.ex: Can I have a pencil, please?
Here you are. It's a red crayon.
Can I have a blue crayon, please?
Can I have some paper, please?

dialogue.t: Can I have a rubber, please?
You're welcome. Can I have a green crayon, please?

grammar.title: Can I have a ..., please?
grammar.ar: نستخدم "Can I have a ..., please?" لنطلب شيئاً بأدب، ومعناها "هل يمكنني أن آخذ ... من فضلك؟". عندما نعطي الشيء نقول "Here you are."، ثم نقول "Thank you."، ويكون الرد "You're welcome.".
examples: Can I have a pencil, please?

dialogue.t: Yes, I do. I like numbers!
I don't like maths. I like art.
My favourite lesson is art. I draw and paint.
Oh! My favourite lesson is music. I sing!

grammar.title: I like ... / I don't like ... / Do you like ...?
grammar.ar: نقول "I like" لما نحبه، و"I don't like" لما لا نحبه. نسأل صديقنا "Do you like ...?" ويكون الجواب "Yes, I do." أو "No, I don't.". ونقول "My favourite lesson is ..." عن الدرس الذي نحبه أكثر من غيره.
examples: I like English. I don't like maths.
Do you like art? Yes, I do.

words.ex: I like grapes. They are yummy.
Do you like carrots? Yes, I do.

dialogue.t: Yes, I do. I like dates!
No, I don't. I don't like bananas.
Yes, I do. Do you like carrots?
Yes, I do. Carrots are good!

grammar.title: I like / I don't like / Do you like?
grammar.ar: نقول I like للتعبير عن شيء نحبه، و I don't like لشيء لا نحبه. للسؤال نبدأ بكلمة Do فنقول: Do you like ...? ونجيب بـ Yes, I do أو No, I don't. انتبه: في العربية لا نستخدم كلمة مثل Do في السؤال، لكن في الإنجليزية هي ضرورية. وغالبًا نستخدم صيغة الجمع بعد like مثل bananas و apples.
examples: Do you like oranges? Yes, I do.

words.ex: I eat breakfast with my family.
For breakfast I have bread and cheese.
I eat cheese in the morning.

dialogue.t: What do you have for breakfast?
For breakfast I have bread and cheese.
Yes, I do. I eat eggs and olives.
I drink milk. My dad drinks tea.
Yummy! I have eggs and juice.

grammar.title: I have / I eat / I drink
grammar.ar: نستخدم For breakfast I have ... and ... لنقول ماذا نأكل في الفطور. نستخدم I eat مع الطعام مثل bread و eggs، و I drink مع المشروبات مثل milk و tea. نستخدم and لنربط بين شيئين.
examples: For breakfast I have bread and eggs.

words.ex: Can I have some juice, please?
Can I have some water, please?
Can I have some rice, please?

dialogue.t: Mum, can I have some juice, please?
Yes, please. Can I have some chicken, please?
Here you are. Do you want some water?

grammar.title: Can I have some ..., please?
grammar.ar: نستخدم Can I have some ..., please? لنطلب طعامًا أو شرابًا بأدب. عندما نعطي شيئًا لشخص نقول Here you are، وهو يرد بـ Thank you. إذا عرض علينا أحد شيئًا نقول Yes, please للقبول أو No, thank you للرفض بأدب.
examples: Can I have some water, please?

words.ex: There are two eggs on the plate.

dialogue.t: Look at the picture. How many apples are there?
Good! How many bananas are there?

grammar.title: How many ... are there? / There is / There are
grammar.ar: نستخدم How many ... are there? لنسأل عن عدد الأشياء، ويأتي بعد How many اسم بصيغة الجمع. نجيب بـ There is one ... إذا كان الشيء واحدًا، و There are ... إذا كان أكثر من واحد. لاحظ أننا نضيف حرف s للجمع مثل apple تصبح apples.

words.ex: I go to the juice shop with my dad.
I'd like a mango juice, please.
I'd like a strawberry juice, please.
I'd like a cheese sandwich, please.
Can I have a cake, please?
I'd like an ice cream, please.

dialogue.t: Hello! I'd like a mango juice, please.
What would you like to eat?
I'd like a cheese sandwich, please.

grammar.title: What would you like? / I'd like ...
grammar.ar: يسأل البائع What would you like? بمعنى ماذا تريد؟ ونجيب بأدب I'd like a ..., please. كلمة I'd like هي اختصار I would like وهي أكثر أدبًا من I want. نستخدم a قبل الاسم المفرد مثل a sandwich، و an قبل الكلمة التي تبدأ بصوت حرف علة مثل an ice cream.
examples: I'd like a strawberry juice, please.
I'd like an ice cream, please.

dialogue.t: My favourite food is chicken and rice.
It's yummy! Teacher, what's your favourite food?
Yes, I do. I love pizza!

grammar.title: My favourite food is ... / What's your favourite food?
grammar.ar: نقول My favourite food is ... لنذكر الطعام الذي نحبه أكثر من غيره. للسؤال نقول What's your favourite food? و What's هي اختصار What is. نستخدم I love عندما نحب شيئًا كثيرًا جدًا، وهي أقوى من I like، ونقول It's yummy عندما يكون الطعام لذيذًا.

words.ex: The duck is on the farm.

dialogue.t: Look at the farm! What's this?

grammar.title: What's this? / What are these?
grammar.ar: نستخدم "What's this?" للسؤال عن شيء واحد، ونجيب بـ "It's a ...". ونستخدم "What are these?" للسؤال عن أكثر من شيء، ونجيب بـ "They're ...". في الجمع نضيف حرف s إلى آخر الاسم غالبًا، مثل cow ← cows. انتبه: كلمة sheep لا تتغير في الجمع.

words.ex: The cow is black and white.

dialogue.t: Is the camel big or small?
It's brown. It's a big brown camel!
Yes! And the chicken is small.

grammar.title: Adjectives before nouns
grammar.ar: في العربية تأتي الصفة بعد الاسم، فنقول: جمل كبير. أما في الإنجليزية فتأتي الصفة قبل الاسم، فنقول: a big camel. وعندما نستخدم صفتين نذكر الحجم أولًا ثم اللون، مثل: a big brown camel. ويمكن أيضًا أن تأتي الصفة بعد is، مثل: The camel is big.

dialogue.t: Watch me! I'm an animal. I can swim.
Yes, it can. A duck can swim and fly.
No, it can't. A cow can't fly!
My turn. Look! I can jump.
Are you a frog? Can a frog jump?
Yes, it can. I'm a frog!

grammar.title: can / can't
grammar.ar: نستخدم can للتعبير عن القدرة على فعل شيء، و can't للتعبير عن عدم القدرة. يأتي الفعل بعد can كما هو بدون إضافة s، فنقول: A bird can fly وليس flies. وللسؤال نضع can في أول الجملة: Can a fish swim? ونجيب: Yes, it can أو No, it can't.
examples: Can a fish swim? Yes, it can.

words.ex: A monkey has got a long tail.
Has it got a long tail?
A rabbit has got a short tail.
A horse has got four legs.

dialogue.t: Has it got a long tail?
No, it hasn't. It's got a short tail.

grammar.title: Has it got ...?
grammar.ar: نستخدم "Has it got ...?" للسؤال عمّا يملكه الحيوان من صفات، مثل الذيل أو الأذنين. الإجابة القصيرة تكون: Yes, it has أو No, it hasn't. ونستخدم "Is it ...?" للسؤال عن الصفة أو عن اسم الحيوان، ونجيب: Yes, it is أو No, it isn't.
examples: Has it got a long tail? Yes, it has.
Has it got big ears? No, it hasn't.
Is it a monkey? Yes, it is.

words.ex: My pet is small and white.
Its name is Snowy. It's a rabbit.

dialogue.t: Its name is Lulu. My pet is small and grey.
I like cats! I haven't got a pet.

grammar.title: I've got / I want / Its
grammar.ar: نقول "I've got a ..." عندما نملك شيئًا فعلًا، ونقول "I want a ..." عندما نرغب في شيء لا نملكه. كلمة Its (بدون فاصلة علوية) تعني "ـه" أي ملكية الحيوان، مثل: Its name is Max أي اسمه ماكس. أما It's فتعني It is.
examples: Its name is Coco. My pet is big and brown.

words.ex: My favourite animal is the lion.

dialogue.t: Welcome to the zoo! Look! It's a lion.
Wow! It's big. Look! It's a monkey.
I like the monkey. It can climb!
I like the giraffe. It's got a long neck.
My favourite animal is the elephant. What's your favourite animal?
My favourite animal is the lion.

grammar.title: My favourite animal is the ...
grammar.ar: نسأل عن الحيوان المفضّل بقولنا: "What's your favourite animal?" ونجيب: "My favourite animal is the ...". ونستخدم "Look! It's a ..." للفت انتباه شخص إلى شيء نراه. كلمة favourite تأتي قبل الاسم، عكس العربية حيث نقول: الحيوان المفضّل.
examples: My favourite animal is the giraffe.

units.cando: Can introduce family members and friends and say simple things about them using basic words and short sentences.
lessons: This Is My Family
Show a family photo to the teacher and name each person.
This is my .... / He is my .... / She is my ....
How Old Is Your Brother?
Ask and answer questions about the ages of family members.
How old is your ...? / He is .... / She is ... years old.
My Best Friend
Talk about a best friend's name and age.
My best friend is .... / His name is .... / Her name is .... / He is ... too.
Who Is Tall?
Describe family members with simple adjectives during a guessing game.
My ... is tall. / My ... is short. / Is he tall? Yes, he is. / No, he isn't.
Have You Got a Sister?
Ask the teacher about brothers and sisters and answer about yourself.
Have you got a ...? / Yes, I have. / No, I haven't. / I've got two ....
Family Day Visit
Role-play greeting relatives at a family gathering and introducing them politely.
Hello, ...! / This is my .... / Nice to meet you. / How are you? I'm fine, thank you.

units.cando: Can name everyday school objects and ask and answer very simple questions about things in the classroom.
lessons: What's in My Bag?
Open a school bag together and name what is inside.
What's in your bag? / I've got a .... / I've got two ....
Is This Your Pencil?
Find the owner of lost school things in a classroom role-play.
Is this your ...? / Yes, it is. / No, it isn't. / It's his .... / It's her ....
What Colour Is It?
Describe the colours of school things in a find-and-show game.
What colour is your ...? / It's .... / My ... is ... and ....
Where Is My Ruler?
Help the teacher find objects in a picture of a classroom.
Where is the ...? / It's in the .... / It's on the .... / It's under the ....
Can I Have a Rubber, Please?
Ask a classmate politely to borrow things during an art activity.
Can I have a ..., please? / Here you are. / Thank you. / You're welcome.
My Favourite Lesson
Talk about favourite school subjects and what you do in class.
I like .... / I don't like .... / My favourite lesson is .... / Do you like ...? Yes, I do. / No, I don't.

units.cando: Can say what food and drinks they like or don't like and make a simple request for food using please and thank you.
lessons: I Like Dates!
Talk about favourite fruits and healthy snacks.
I like .... / I don't like .... / Do you like ...? Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
What's for Breakfast?
Describe a family breakfast table and what you eat in the morning.
For breakfast I have ... and .... / I eat .... / I drink ....
Can I Have Some Juice?
Role-play asking for food and drinks at the dinner table.
Can I have some ..., please? / Here you are. / Thank you. / Yes, please. / No, thank you.
How Many Apples?
Count food items in a picture and answer questions about them.
